newsitem.title: THAILAND: Top four Thai banks still sound buys - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Top four Thai banks still sound buys - analysts.

text.p: Stocks of Thailand's top four banks are still attractive buys despite a recent gloomy assessment of the entire banking sector by rating agency Capital Intelligence, analysts said on Tuesday.

The Cyprus-based rating agency assigned negative outlooks to all Thai banks on Friday, saying Thailand's slowing economic growth and current political instability would increase the vulnerability of the banking system to external shocks.
But analysts told Reuters that the rating agency had failed to reflect the dominant position of the top banks.

Analysts said the agency's warning would apply more to Thailand's 11 domestic medium and smaller banks who are under pressure from increased funding costs and the erosion of lending opportunities due an economic slowdown.
"I think Capital Intelligence's report is very short term," said Man Joavishida, a banking analyst at Asia Credit, "I think the stocks of the leading banks are quite cheap."
The four solid buys, based also on their continuing profitability, were Bangkok Bank Plc, Krung Thai Bank Plc, Thai Farmers Bank Plc and Siam Commercial Bank Plc, analysts added.
"The top four Thai banks operate a virtual cartel, and they continue to make profits even when the economy is slowing," said another banking analyst.
Average half-year profits for these banks increased by more than 10 percent year-on-year despite the deteriorating economy, analysts said.
That view was supported by Merrill Lynch & Co Inc, which last Friday included Thai Farmers Bank as one of its 17 top picks in international banking stocks.
Analysts said the stocks of the top four banks were heavily favoured by institutional and foreign investors who have had long time holdings in them.
They argued that the average price earnings ratios of 12.1 for the four banks, while marginally above the total market average of 10.2, were still attractive.
Shares of the top banks have out-performed the bearish market since the start of 1996 and have held their value during the period.
For example, shares of the nation's biggest bank, Bangkok Bank, closed on Monday at 216 baht, and Krung Thai Bank, which began the year at 104 baht, has also generally held steady.
Over the same period, the Thai stock index has dropped 230 points, or 16.9 percent, on growing disappointment with the economy and concerns over the country's political stability.

Private analysts have forecast Thai gross domestic product growth will slow to below 7.0 percent from 8.6 percent in 1995 based on slack exports growth, private investment and industrial production indices this year.
The government's handling of economic and domestic political issues has been sharply attacked by the opposition and the local media.

Debate will begin on Wednesday on an opposition-tabled no-confidence motion against Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa. The motion charges him with incompetence and economic mismanagement, which he has denied.
All eyes are on Banharn's 14-month-old, six-party coalition government to see if it will weather the storm.
